title: Testing the Artificial Hivemind Effect on Structured Safety Reasoning Tasks

original_idea.title: Testing the Artificial Hivemind Effect on Structured Safety Reasoning Tasks
original_idea.problem: The original Artificial Hivemind paper tested open-ended generative tasks. It is unknown whether the same homogeneity effect holds for structured safety reasoning tasks.
original_idea.direction: Use the Infinity-Chat methodology -- pairwise semantic similarity across models -- but replace open-ended queries with a curated set of safety reasoning tasks. Measure whether homogeneity coefficients are higher, lower, or the same.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Safety reasoning tasks are more directly consequential than creative tasks; establishing whether homogeneity carries over is a direct safety research priority.
original_idea.relevant_context: Infinity-Chat benchmark (26K queries, 31K annotations, 70+ models); AILuminate safety hazard categories provide a ready-made task bank.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: directly extends the Artificial Hivemind finding to safety-relevant tasks, which are more consequential. A positive finding has immediate safety implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: replicating the Infinity-Chat methodology with new task types requires understanding the protocol and analysis pipeline, but the original paper provides guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: homogeneity coefficients on safety reasoning tasks compared to original open-ended baseline, with a clear numerical comparison.

novelty.reasoning: The Artificial Hivemind paper explicitly tested open-ended generative tasks only. The extension to structured safety reasoning tasks is a natural but unstudied follow-up. The paper itself suggests safety-relevant extensions as future work. No existing study applies the Infinity-Chat homogeneity measurement protocol to safety reasoning.

evidence.finding: Documents pronounced inter-model homogeneity across 70+ LLMs on open-ended generative tasks using Infinity-Chat (26K queries). Does NOT test structured safety reasoning tasks.
Provides 24K+ safety test prompts across 12 hazard categories, which could serve as the task bank for this study.
